messages.content:
You are a blind semantic decoder of a natural-language crystal description. The user message is your only source of material-specific information. Understand the spatial narrative and produce a construction plan; do not guess missing independent numbers or look up a material. Return one JSON object only, without Markdown fences.
For sufficient information use:
{"status":"ok","space_group_number":integer,"hall_symbol":"Hall symbol stated in the text","lattice":[input_a,input_b,input_c,input_alpha,input_beta,input_gamma],"composition":{"Element":input_cell_atom_count},"orbits":[{"element":"Element","wyckoff":"multiplicity_and_letter","representative":[standard_fractional_x,standard_fractional_y,standard_fractional_z]}],"frame_transform":{"matrix":[[p11,p12,p13],[p21,p22,p23],[p31,p32,p33]],"origin_shift":[s1,s2,s3]},"round_digits":integer_or_null,"precision_corrections":[{"element":"Element","at":[input_fractional_x_before_correction,input_fractional_y_before_correction,input_fractional_z_before_correction],"delta":[fractional_dx,fractional_dy,fractional_dz]}]}
Lengths use angstroms, angles use degrees. The specified lattice and composition refer to the original input cell. Orbit representatives refer to the standard Hall coordinate frame. Copy the Hall symbol as a mathematical identifier rather than guessing a public-table integer number. Any equivalent representative of a declared orbit is allowed. Distinct independent orbits of the same element remain separate.
The geometry engine expands the public Hall symmetry orbits, applies q_input = inverse(P)(q_standard - s), selects images in the input cell, rounds fractional coordinates if round_digits is given, and applies precision corrections at their identified input-frame atom positions. If the text explicitly uses identical frames, supply identity P and zero shift. If no rounding is specified, use null. If no corrections are specified, use an empty array. All sites have full occupancy.
Numerical relations in the prose should be resolved into numbers in the plan. Do not silently replace the original geometry with an idealized one. For missing required information return {"status":"insufficient_information","reason":"..."}; for contradictory constraints return {"status":"conflict","reason":"..."}. Your input contains no source CIF or hidden data. Public crystallographic definitions are allowed; material-specific external retrieval is not.

The structure is described in space group R3 (number 146, Hall symbol R 3), a rhombohedral setting with threefold rotational symmetry about the c axis and rhombohedral centering. The input cell is a primitive rhombohedral cell with all three lattice parameters equal to approximately 7.1999 Å (a = b = c = 7.1999035, 7.1999035, and 7.19990343 Å) and all three interaxial angles equal to about 115.3734° (α = β = γ = 115.37341955°, 115.37341955°, and 115.3734177°). This input cell contains 11 atoms with the composition Sn₃P₁O₄F₃.

The relationship between the input frame and the standard crystallographic frame is given by q_standard = P q_input + s, where the transformation matrix P has rows (2/3, −1/3, −1/3), (1/3, 1/3, −2/3), and (1/3, 1/3, 1/3), and the origin shift s is (0, 0, 0). This transformation converts fractional coordinates from the primitive rhombohedral input cell to the standard rhombohedral setting used for the Wyckoff orbit descriptions.

Within the standard frame, the structure contains five independent atomic orbits. Tin occupies a single ninefold general position, Wyckoff site 9b, with the representative atom at fractional coordinates (x, y, z) = (0.215779, 0.432493, 0.155811). The threefold rotation about c and the rhombohedral centering generate the full set of nine equivalent Sn atoms per standard cell from this single representative.

Phosphorus sits on the threefold axis at Wyckoff site 3a, with coordinates (0, 0, z) where z = 0.991407. This places P essentially at the cell origin along c, displaced slightly from z = 0. The threefold symmetry and centering generate three equivalent P atoms.

There are two crystallographically distinct oxygen sublattices. The first oxygen orbit also lies on the threefold axis at Wyckoff site 3a, with coordinates (0, 0, z) where z = 0.325381, giving three equivalent O atoms positioned roughly one-third of the way along the c axis. The second oxygen orbit occupies the ninefold general position 9b, with the representative atom at (x, y, z) = (0.140623, 0.070195, 0.895024). This generates nine equivalent O atoms distributed throughout the cell.

Fluorine occupies a ninefold general position, Wyckoff site 9b, with the representative atom at (x, y, z) = (0.065590, 0.594545, 0.109903). The threefold rotation and rhombohedral centering produce nine equivalent F atoms from this representative.

All fractional coordinates are reported to six decimal places. No precision corrections were applied to the input coordinates; the listed values represent the original input geometry. The complete structure thus consists of these five independent orbits—one Sn site, one P site, two distinct O sites, and one F site—arranged according to the R3 symmetry within the rhombohedral cell.
